Doc1
Working title: Decks & Dungeons

Fantasy themed rogue-like deck builder with an emphasis on co-op play
Different classes themed after classes in Dungeons & Dragons. Warrior (barbarian and fighter) , Rogue, Ranger (Ranger and druid), Cleric, Guardian (Paladin), Mage (Sorcerer and Wizard) , Warlock, Monk and Bard. Each class has subclasses that will change some of the starting cards, equipment, and talents that the class uses.

Mechanics

Each deck starts with 10 cards, 1 equipment, and 1 Talent. Cards are earned after battles, equipment is earned after special events, and talents are learned with xp that is awarded with every action. (some actions give more than others) Players will proceed through different stages of a randomly generated dungeon, alone or with a team, completing card battles and random events as they go along and improving their combat power with new cards, removing old cards, getting equipment, and leveling up to get new talents and stats.

The game consists of several different zones that are accessed with portals. This allows us to put the party against goblins in a small cave and still fight demons in the 9th dimension of hell later on. Snowy mountains, underwater cities, lush jungles or whatever else we want to include complete with unique events, equipment, monsters and bosses.

As parties navigate these zones they will be provided with a limited amount of information. The final boss of each zone will be given to them with flavor text when entering a zone. For example the party sees a young red dragon fly overhead and land near the top of the mountain area the party just portaled into. At the top of the mountain they can see the blue glow of the next portal. The party then will see a map navigating them to the top of the mountain but each space will only be revealed to them as they get 1 space away from it. This will allow parties to avoid certain challenging fights but not plan too far ahead as to avoid every difficulty within the adventure. Certain items or talents would increase the parties scouting range allowing them to see spaces 2 or more spaces in advance.

Battle

Battles are split up into just 2 phases, player phase and enemy phase. During the player phase, all players will take their turn simultaneously. This will require teamwork and strategy from the players in order to work as efficiently as possible. This will increase the emphasis on Cooperation as well as minimize dead time in which the players aren’t taking any actions. The worst part about playing multiplayer turn based games is waiting through 4 or 5 turns till you get to take your turn. Most of the game you aren’t actually doing anything. So we won’t have multiple turns to keep the game pace quicker and more exciting. There also isn’t a time limit so if parties want to slow down and strategize they are free to do so if that fits their play style more. It may seem hard to navigate turns at first but the more runs players do the easier it will be to be efficient in combat with your party.

Progression

One of the staples of a rouge-like game is progression from run to run. Unlocking equipment, classes, subclasses, cards and other permanent additions to each run. The other important part is learning all the encounters and events within each run and exploring what the game has to offer. These two things give rouge-likes their replay value and the more of it we have the more valuable the game is.

Unlocking 
Players will only start with 1 class, the Warior. After completing the first area the ranger is unlocked as well. More classes and subclasses are unlocked for completing different challenges. Completing X runs, beating the game, killing X enemies with a certain class, completing certain events, and so on. Cosmetics can be unlocked for completing challenge runs. Examples are card backs for Challenge 5 Skins for challenge 10 and different style foil cards for beating challenge 5,10,20 using a card in your deck. As you play through and discover new cards and equipment they will be logged into a catalog (cool name needed) that can be viewed.

This will require teamwork and strategy from the players in order to work as efficiently as possible. This will increase the emphasis on Cooperation as well as minimize dead time in which the players aren’t taking any actions. It may seem hard to navigate turns at first but the more runs players do the easier it will be to be efficient in combat with your party.

Idea: Coop version of the game has “Coop” only cards that must be played concurrently with a teammate’s “Coop” card. This forces cooperation as well as enhancing the multiplayer feel of the game. 3 possible interactions with these cards:

1. Card can only be played if your teammate has a “coop” card queued to be played.

2. Card can be played on its own, but if the turn ends without a teammates coop card, it has a reduced or negative effect.

3. Card can be “played” on its own, but does nothing but burn mana if your teammate doesn’t play a coop card.

Progression

One of the staples of a rouge-like game is progression from run to run. Unlocking equipment, classes, subclasses, cards and other permanent additions to each run. The other important part is learning all the encounters and events within each run and exploring what the game has to offer. These two things give rouge-likes their replay value and the more of it we have the more valuable the game is.

Unlocking 
Players will only start with 1 class, the Warior. After completing the first area the ranger is unlocked as well. More classes and subclasses are unlocked for completing different challenges. Completing X runs, beating the game, killing X enemies with a certain class, completing certain events, and so on. Cosmetics can be unlocked for completing challenge runs. Examples are card backs for Challenge 5 Skins for challenge 10 and different style foil cards for beating challenge 5,10,20 using a card in your deck. As you play through and discover new cards and equipment they will be logged into a catalog (cool name needed) that can be viewed.

Exploring
The game will be separated into 3 stages each increasing in difficulty. Each stage is largely randomized allowing for more replayability within the game. Not only are the encounters and bosses within a given stage randomized but the stage itself also will be randomized. There will be a set of starter stages, mid stages, and end stages. Each one will be chosen randomly unless the party has a benefit that allows them to control or partially control stage selection.

1st stage ideas: Echo Caves, Thieves City

Echo Caves: Your generic starting adventure from a fantasy game. Groups of goblins, orcs, slimes, bandits, spiders and the like. Bosses range from Orc chiefs to goblin hordes to a dark elf up to no good. Events include fungi overrun rooms, tunnel mazes, underground lakes, and old abandoned rooms like kitchens and barracks or armories.

Thieves City: A dangerous city filled with bandits, giant rats, ravenous stray dogs, cultists, and some other low lifes. Bosses can include bandit leaders, cultists leaders, and a werewolf. Events range from encounters with beggars asking for money to shady stores and dark alleyways.

2nd Stage Ideas: Necropolis, Red mountains, Jungle (name needed desperately)

Necropolis: A graveyard with an underground crypt as well as above ground cemetery section. There will be skeletons. Also zombies, ghosts, necromancers and such. Bosses include a lich, a bone dragon.

Red mountains: A vast and dangerous mountain range with many strange beasts to fight. Land sharks, ogres, and red drakes can be encountered here. Bosses include a red dragon, a lava elemental.

Jungle: an extremely dense jungle with many challenges. Giant panthers, giant mosquito swarms, carnivorous plants,

3rd Stage Ideas: Atlantis, Shadow Realm, Hell dimension

Atlantis: The fabled underwater city is mostly abandoned after a parasite turned all of its fishy humanoid residents insane. A few atlanteans can still be found around as well as golem constructions, mutated sharks, and other ocean beasts. Bosses range from a kraken, to the crazed king of atlantis. Events can be a still sane (kinda) atlantean scientist, an old atlantean armory, the city square (now filled with corpses) and others.

Shadow Realm: a dark version of our reality kinda like the upside down. The city in which our heroes start is the setting but shadow version. Heroes can encounter shadow elementals, mind flayers (the dnd kind), and more. Bosses include a shadow party (dark link versions of themselves) and more.

Hell Dimension: Yeah it's just what it sounds like. Many different kinds of demons, imp hoards, hell hounds and more are battles here. Bosses include a chain demon, Cerberus,

Vanilla (Fighter)
10 cards: strikeX4 blockX3 surgeX1 Fighters WillX1 (coop) Combo StrikeX1 (solo) Deadly StrikeX1

Ranger

Other

Main Screen
The game's main screen is a tavern. This is where players can invite people to form a party, select their character and subclass, view the cardopedia, and maybe play some other mini games or some shit. After each achievement unlocked in the game, something new can be added to the tavern. Characters not currently selected will idle in the tavern, after killing a dragon boss a mounted dragon head will appear on the wall and things like that.

Music
We have some choices for music. We can compose our own stuff or pay a contractor to compose some music for us or let us use theirs. We also have the option of using classical music in our game. This music isn’t copyrighted because it was made so long ago so as long as we either perform it ourselves or get permission for use to use someone else's recording we could do this option. I have a roland FX-30 piano keyboard that can be linked computers to record high quality music and Emily is a fantastic piano player who can perform practically any song as long as she has a day or two to practice. This means our game wouldn’t have music early on since she isn’t here currently but I think we could do this fairly easily.

Art
IDK man. I know a decent artist but I know little to nothing about game art and if she would be capable of doing something like that. Right now I think our best option for the art is to find someone else that is capable of doing something like that and contracting that work out.

Takeaway Items 11/1

- Platform (Unreal Engine, etc)

	- Unreal Engine: No royalties on first $1,000,000. After that, charged quarterly at 5% IF revenue > $10,000 in that quarter.

	- Unity Engine: No royalties ever. Free if ENTIRE organization is making < $100,000 per year. $399 per license (per person) if ENTIRE organization making > $100,000 and < $200,000 per year. $2,040 if ENTIRE organization making > $200,000 per year. NOTE THAT this is based on tax statements and therefore INCLUDES fundraising completely unrelated to Unity Engine.

- Hosting solution (Native, etc)

- Task planning and accountability solution

- Prototype Title Screen/Main Menu

- Flush out vanilla classes (cards+talents+equipment)

- Learn more about marketing

- What type of business is this? What model?

- Card tracking system

Working title: Decks & Dungeons

Fantasy themed rogue-like deck builder with an emphasis on co-op play
Different classes themed after classes in Dungeons & Dragons. Warrior (barbarian and fighter) , Rogue, Ranger (Ranger and druid), Cleric, Guardian (Paladin), Mage (Sorcerer and Wizard) , Warlock, Monk and Bard. Each class has subclasses that will change some of the starting cards, equipment, and talents that the class uses. Examples include Fighter (Spellblade) that would gain access to wizard cards and have a talent increasing spell damage after dealing melee damage and vice versa.
We could also include races for each class to choose from as well.

Mechanics

Each deck starts with 10 cards, 1 equipment, and 1 Talent. Cards are earned after battles, equipment is earned after special events, and talents are learned with xp that is awarded with every action. (some actions give more than others) Players will proceed through different stages of a randomly generated dungeon, alone or with a team, completing card battles and random events as they go along and improving their combat power with new cards, removing old cards, getting equipment, and leveling up to get new talents and stats.

The game consists of several different zones that are accessed with portals. This allows us to put the party against goblins in a small cave and still fight demons in the 9th dimension of hell later on. Snowy mountains, underwater cities, lush jungles or whatever else we want to include complete with unique events, equipment, monsters and bosses.

As parties navigate these zones they will be provided with a limited amount of information. The final boss of each zone will be given to them with flavor text when entering a zone. For example the party sees a young red dragon fly overhead and land near the top of the mountain area the party just portaled into. At the top of the mountain they can see the blue glow of the next portal. The party then will see a map navigating them to the top of the mountain but each space will only be revealed to them as they get 1 space away from it. This will allow parties to avoid certain challenging fights but not plan too far ahead as to avoid every difficulty within the adventure. Certain items or talents would increase the parties scouting range allowing them to see spaces 2 or more spaces in advance.

Battle

Battles are split up into just 2 phases, player phase and enemy phase. During the player phase, all players will take their turn simultaneously. This will require teamwork and strategy from the players in order to work as efficiently as possible. This will increase the emphasis on Cooperation as well as minimize dead time in which the players aren’t taking any actions. The worst part about playing multiplayer turn based games is waiting through 4 or 5 turns till you get to take your turn. Most of the game you aren’t actually doing anything. So we won’t have multiple turns to keep the game pace quicker and more exciting. There also isn’t a time limit so if parties want to slow down and strategize they are free to do so if that fits their play style more. It may seem hard to navigate turns at first but the more runs players do the easier it will be to be efficient in combat with your party.

Idea: Coop version of the game has “Coop” only cards that must be played concurrently with a teammate’s “Coop” card. This forces cooperation as well as enhancing the multiplayer feel of the game. 3 possible interactions with these cards:

1. Card can only be played if your teammate has a “coop” card queued to be played.

2. Card can be played on its own, but if the turn ends without a teammates coop card, it has a reduced or negative effect.

3. Card can be “played” on its own, but does nothing but burn mana if your teammate doesn’t play a coop card.

Progression

One of the staples of a rouge-like game is progression from run to run. Unlocking equipment, classes, subclasses, cards and other permanent additions to each run. The other important part is learning all the encounters and events within each run and exploring what the game has to offer. These two things give rouge-likes their replay value and the more of it we have the more valuable the game is.

Unlocking 
Players will only start with 1 class, the Warior. After completing the first area the ranger is unlocked as well. More classes and subclasses are unlocked for completing different challenges. Completing X runs, beating the game, killing X enemies with a certain class, completing certain events, and so on. Cosmetics can be unlocked for completing challenge runs. Examples are card backs for Challenge 5 Skins for challenge 10 and different style foil cards for beating challenge 5,10,20 using a card in your deck. As you play through and discover new cards and equipment they will be logged into a catalog (cool name needed) that can be viewed.

Exploring
The game will be separated into 3 stages each increasing in difficulty. Each stage is largely randomized allowing for more replayability within the game. Not only are the encounters and bosses within a given stage randomized but the stage itself also will be randomized. There will be a set of starter stages, mid stages, and end stages. Each one will be chosen randomly unless the party has a benefit that allows them to control or partially control stage selection.

1st stage ideas: Forgotten Mines, Thieves City

Forgotten Mines: Your generic starting adventure from a fantasy game. Groups of goblins, orcs, slimes, bandits, spiders and the like. Bosses range from Orc chiefs to goblin hordes to a dark elf up to no good. Events include fungi overrun rooms, tunnel mazes, underground lakes, and old abandoned rooms like kitchens and barracks or armories.

Thieves City: A dangerous city filled with bandits, giant rats, ravenous stray dogs, cultists, and some other low lifes. Bosses can include bandit leaders, cultists leaders, and a werewolf. Events range from encounters with beggars asking for money to shady stores and dark alleyways.

2nd Stage Ideas: Necropolis, Red mountains, Jungle (name needed desperately)

Necropolis: A graveyard with an underground crypt as well as above ground cemetery section. There will be skeletons. Also zombies, ghosts, necromancers and such. Bosses include a lich, a bone dragon.

Red mountains: A vast and dangerous mountain range with many strange beasts to fight. Land sharks, ogres, and red drakes can be encountered here. Bosses include a red dragon, a lava elemental.

Jungle: an extremely dense jungle with many challenges. Giant panthers, giant mosquito swarms, carnivorous plants,

3rd Stage Ideas: Atlantis, Shadow Realm, Hell dimension, Celestial Realm

Atlantis: The fabled underwater city is mostly abandoned after a parasite turned all of its fishy humanoid residents insane. A few atlanteans can still be found around as well as golem constructions, mutated sharks, and other ocean beasts. Bosses range from a kraken, to the crazed king of atlantis. Events can be a still sane (kinda) atlantean scientist, an old atlantean armory, the city square (now filled with corpses) and others.

Shadow Realm: a dark version of our reality kinda like the upside down. The city in which our heroes start is the setting but shadow version. Heroes can encounter shadow elementals, mind flayers (the dnd kind), and more. Bosses include a shadow party (dark link versions of themselves) and more.

Hell Dimension: Yeah it's just what it sounds like. Many different kinds of demons, imp hoards, hell hounds and more are battles here. Bosses include a chain demon, Cerberus,
